1.subtopic: Say Hello to the Home Row Keys
1.outline: Term theme: 'My First Words on Screen'. Recap sitting posture and finger position. Find ASDF and JKL; with eyes closed, then start the first Term 2 TypingClub unit.
1.sowResources: TypingClub, posture poster, printed keyboard mat.
objectives: Sit with good posture and find the home row without looking.
Complete a TypingClub unit using only home-row keys.
Set a small personal typing goal for Term 2.

plan.title: Posture and home row recap
plan.detail: Chant the posture rule, then find F and J with eyes closed three times.

plan.title: Home row unit
plan.detail: Work through a TypingClub home-row unit, freezing every 5 minutes for a posture check.

plan.title: Term 2 goal
plan.detail: Write one typing goal for this term on the goal sheet — a star count or a level.

plan.title: Show a partner
plan.detail: Show a partner your fingers finding the home row without looking. Log out.

successCriteria: I can find F and J without looking.
I completed a home-row typing unit.
I have written a typing goal for this term.

2.outline: Recap that Word and Google Docs do the same job, two different ways. Open both, type first name in each, and save with a sensible name.
2.sowResources: Microsoft Word, Google Docs, class login cards.
objectives: Open both Microsoft Word and Google Docs.
Type my name in each program.
Save each file with my name.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes of TypingClub, posture check.

plan.title: Two tools, one job
plan.detail: Recap the Word/Docs comparison from Year 1's earlier work: same buttons, different shop.

plan.title: Open and type
plan.detail: Open Word, type name, save. Then open Docs, type name — notice it saves itself.

plan.title: Show and tell
plan.detail: Show a partner both files open side by side. Log out.

successCriteria: I opened both Word and Google Docs.
I typed my name correctly in each.
Both files are saved with my name.

3.subtopic: Use the Shift Key for Capital Letters
3.outline: Practise holding Shift and pressing a letter to make a capital. Type first and last name, each starting with a capital.
3.sowResources: Microsoft Word, Google Docs, printed name cards.
objectives: Use the Shift key to make a capital letter.
Type my first and last name correctly.
Explain when a word needs a capital letter.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Shift key practice
plan.detail: Air-practise 'hold Shift, press letter, let go' before touching the keyboard.

plan.title: Type my full name
plan.detail: Type first and last name in Word and Docs, each starting with a capital letter.

plan.title: Capital hunt
plan.detail: Spot capital letters in a printed sentence and say why each one is there. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I can use Shift to make a capital letter.
My first and last name both start with capitals.
I can point to a capital letter and say why it's there.

4.subtopic: Spaces and Full Stops Make Sense
4.outline: Type a short sentence about myself, using the space bar correctly between words and a full stop at the end.
4.sowResources: Microsoft Word, Google Docs, printed sentence starters.
objectives: Use the space bar once between each word.
End my sentence with a full stop.
Read my sentence back and check it makes sense.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What makes a sentence
plan.detail: Read example sentences on the board; count the words and spot the full stop.

plan.title: Type my sentence
plan.detail: Type one sentence about myself, e.g. 'My name is ___ and I like ___.' One space between words, full stop at the end.

plan.title: Read-back check
plan.detail: Read the sentence aloud to a partner — does it make sense? Save and log out.

successCriteria: My sentence has one space between each word.
My sentence ends with a full stop.
My sentence makes sense when read aloud.

5.subtopic: Change the Font Size of My Title
5.outline: Select the title of my sentence and make it bigger using the font size dropdown, so it stands out from the rest of the text.
5.sowResources: Microsoft Word, Google Docs, font-size cheat sheet.
objectives: Select a word or line of text.
Change the font size using the toolbar.
Explain why a title should look different from the body text.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Selecting text
plan.detail: Practise clicking and dragging to select a word, then a whole line.

plan.title: Make it big
plan.detail: Add a title above the sentence, select it, and change the font size to something much bigger.

plan.title: Compare
plan.detail: Compare with a partner — does the bigger title stand out? Save and log out.

successCriteria: I can select text by clicking and dragging.
My title is a bigger font size than the body text.
I can explain why a big title is easier to spot.

6.outline: Select the title again and use the font colour tool to give it a colour that is still easy to read.
6.sowResources: Microsoft Word, Google Docs, readable-colours poster.
objectives: Use the font colour tool to change text colour.
Choose a colour that is still easy to read.
Explain why yellow-on-white is hard to read.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Readable or not?
plan.detail: Show two colour examples — one easy to read, one hard. Vote and discuss why.

plan.title: Colour my title
plan.detail: Select the title and apply a font colour. Try two or three colours before choosing the best one.

plan.title: Class gallery
plan.detail: Project three examples — which colours work best and why? Save and log out.

activities: Apply a font colour to the title
successCriteria: I changed my title's colour using the toolbar.
My title colour is still easy to read.
I can say why some colour combinations are hard to read.

7.subtopic: Save to Drive and to OneDrive; Reopen It
7.outline: Practise the full save routine: save the Word file to OneDrive and the Docs file to Drive, then close everything and reopen both to prove it worked.
7.sowResources: Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, file-naming poster.
objectives: Save a file to OneDrive and a file to Drive.
Use a sensible file name.
Close and reopen my own files.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Naming rule recap
plan.detail: Recap Firstname_Topic naming from Year 1 Term 1. Rename today's files to follow the rule.

plan.title: Save to both clouds
plan.detail: Save the Word file to OneDrive and the Docs file stays in Drive automatically. Check both are really there.

plan.title: Close and reopen
plan.detail: Close both files completely, then reopen them from the cloud to prove the save worked. Log out.

successCriteria: My files are named sensibly.
One file is saved in OneDrive and one in Drive.
I reopened both files after closing them.

8.outline: Bring together everything this term: type a one-line 'about me' sentence, make the title big and coloured, and save it to both clouds as the term's portfolio piece.
8.sowResources: Microsoft Word, Google Docs, portfolio folder.
objectives: Type a one-line sentence about myself.
Format the title with size and colour.
Save the finished piece to both clouds.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Plan my sentence
plan.detail: Say the sentence out loud to a partner before typing it.

plan.title: Build the piece
plan.detail: Type the sentence, add a big coloured title, check spaces and full stop.

plan.title: Save to portfolio
plan.detail: Save to both OneDrive and Drive with the correct name, into the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: My sentence is about me and makes sense.
My title is bigger and coloured.
My piece is saved to both clouds in the portfolio folder.

9.subtopic: Add a Picture to My 'About Me'
9.outline: Return to the 'about me' sentence and add a picture — a self-portrait drawing or a copyright-safe image — so the finished piece has words and a picture together.
9.sowResources: Tux Paint / Microsoft Paint, class picture folder, Microsoft Word / Google Docs.
objectives: Draw or choose a picture for my 'about me' piece.
Insert the picture next to my sentence.
Resize the picture so it fits neatly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Picture choice
plan.detail: Choose: draw a quick self-portrait in Paint, or pick a picture from the class folder.

plan.title: Insert and resize
plan.detail: Insert the picture into the document and resize it using the corner handles so it doesn't cover the text.

plan.title: Check together
plan.detail: Partner check: does the picture fit neatly? Save and log out.

activities: Insert and resize into the document
successCriteria: I chose or drew a picture for my piece.
My picture is inserted next to my sentence.
My picture is resized neatly, not squashed.

10.outline: Recap the whole term: open a program, type a sentence with capitals and a full stop, format a title, insert a picture, and save to both clouds. Rehearse in pairs.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards, Microsoft Word / Google Docs.
objectives: Recall every skill learned this term in order.
Rehearse the practical task with a partner.
Identify which step I still find tricky.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Skill recap
plan.detail: Recap slide deck: open, type, format, picture, save — in order, as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: One partner does the full task while the other reads the task card aloud, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Each pupil names the step they still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's skills in order.
I completed the practical task with a partner's help.
I know which step I need more practice on.

11.outline: Individual task: open a program, type a short sentence with a capital letter and a full stop, make the title big and coloured, insert a picture, and save to both clouds.
objectives: Complete the Term 2 practical task independently.
Use everything learned this term: typing, formatting, a picture, saving.
Save my finished work with the correct name.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain this is a 'show me what you can do' task.

plan.title: Group A practical
plan.detail: First group works through the task while others do independent TypingClub.

plan.title: Group B practical
plan.detail: Second group, same task, same checklist.

plan.title: Save and celebrate
plan.detail: Final saves checked, then celebrate the whole class's progress since January. Log out.

activities: Individual observed practical: type, format, picture, save
successCriteria: I typed a sentence with a capital and a full stop on my own.
I formatted my title with size and colour.
I inserted a picture and saved to both clouds.
